claim.quote: First physics results from this method are reported, based on a small 2.3 litre test chamber filled with natural Argon and an accumulated fiducial exposure of about 100 kg x day

key_value_text.note: The paper states its limit as a plotted curve of the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section in cm2 against WIMP mass (Fig. 8; Section 4, Results) and gives no single number, so `key_value` stays empty. Section 1 says the paper will 'report a first upper limit for the WIMP search with sensitivity comparable to the best published result'. The 'about 100 kg x day' of the abstract (96.5 kg x day, 52.76 days live, in Section 4) is the exposure behind the limit, now in `summary.technical`, not the limit; the record used it as its key value until 2026-10-29.
key_value_text.quote: 90 % C.L. spin independent limits (solid blue curve) obtained by WARP-2.3l for a total fiducial exposure of 96.5 kg·d and a threshold of 55 keV.
key_value_text.value: 90% C.L. spin-independent WIMP-nucleon upper limit as a function of WIMP mass, plotted in Fig. 8 (96.5 kg d, 55 keV threshold).

name: First results from a Dark Matter search with liquid Argon at 87 K in the Gran Sasso Underground Laboratory
notes: result_type is 'limit' because the paper's introduction states it reports a first upper limit; the abstract itself gives no limit value (the 2013 review quotes 1e-42 cm^2 for the WIMP-nucleon cross section but that number is not recorded here).
key_value_text is quoted from the paper's introduction (Sec. 1), not from the abstract.

summary.plain: The first dark matter search results from a two-phase liquid argon detector: a 2.3-litre chamber run underground at Gran Sasso for about 100 kg-days.
summary.technical: First WIMP-search results of the WArP method (simultaneous scintillation and ionisation signals) with a 2.3 l chamber of natural argon (96.5 kg d, 52.76 days live in the body of the paper). The body derives a 90% C.L. upper limit from zero events above 55 keV_ion and compares it with CDMS, EDELWEISS and CRESST; the abstract states no number.

title: First results from a Dark Matter search with liquid Argon at 87 K in the Gran Sasso Underground Laboratory
why_it_matters: The abstract says it supports the future validity of the method with isotopically purified 40Ar and with a much larger unit then under construction.
